summary:
[trial 1]: Bitcoin at $95K is only 5.3% below the $100K threshold with 8 months of runway; pure volatility math (σ≈70%) implies a ~93% barrier-touch probability. However, April 2026 is roughly 24 months post-halving, which historically is past the cycle peak — BTC may already have printed its high and be in a distribution or early-decline phase. Repeated failure to breach $100K would reinforce technical resistance, and macro tail risks (credit stress, regulatory action) add further left-skew. Netting these cycle-timing and structural concerns against the proximity-and-time advantage, the probability of at least one daily close above $100K before December 31, 2026 is approximately 0.70.

[trial 2]: Bitcoin at ~$95,000 requires only a 5.3% gain to cross $100K with 8 months remaining, but the setup is more contested than the proximity implies. The cycle context is bearish: the post-halving peak likely occurred in October 2025 (~$126K), and BTC corrected 40%+ before recovering to current levels — classic Year 3 pattern. Conservative analyst consensus places the December 2026 close at $84K–$89K, explicitly below $100K. Offsetting this, spot ETF institutional flows (~$230M/day) represent a structural demand shift that partially invalidates traditional cycle analysis. The USD inverse correlation (-0.90) means dollar weakness or Fed rate cuts would provide meaningful tailwind. On balance, the short distance to $100K, high annualized volatility (~80%), and institutional bid tip the probability modestly above 50%, but cycle exhaustion and analyst consensus keep it well below certainty.

[trial 3]: Bitcoin closed at ~$95K last week, sitting only 5.3% below the $100K threshold with 8 months of runway — a favorable setup on pure volatility math. However, prediction markets price this at 35–40%, reflecting two structural bearish factors: the 2024 halving produced the weakest post-halving rally on record (~31% in year one), suggesting market maturation is dampening the typical cycle amplitude, and Bitcoin has already repeatedly tested and failed to hold $100K, establishing it as durable psychological resistance. Macro tailwinds (ETF inflows, possible Fed cuts, 401(k) regulatory clarity) partially offset these headwinds. The question resolves on any daily close above $100K before December 31, which widens the opportunity window considerably versus a point-in-time condition. Weighing the small required move and long time horizon against weakening cycle dynamics and strong resistance, I estimate 0.63 — materially above prediction markets due to the starting proximity, but well below what naive volatility math would suggest.
